notes:
- Back moves the way you came: Popping a page used to reveal the page underneath from the same edge the pushed page had entered from, so Settings slid in from the right and Back slid the dashboard in from the right too - both halves of one gesture moving the same way. A pop is the push read backwards now: the page being popped leaves to the right and the page underneath enters from the left. Tab pops keep their own direction, which already came from the bar's order.
- The demo profile keeps Home behind it: Opening Profile in the demo used to replace the demo dashboard instead of stacking on it, which left the profile alone on the back stack. Its back arrow did nothing, and a Home/Profile round trip pushed a duplicate profile each time, so Back walked through copies of the same page. Profile is a tab in both sessions now, and every tab keeps the demo dashboard underneath it.
- A tab switch leaves the graph alone: The main bar and the joke toast used to read the current route in the same scope that calls the navigation graph, so every push, pop and tab switch re-ran the graph's destination table to move two overlays. Each host reads the route in its own scope now; a route change redraws the bar and the toast, not the screens behind them.
- Seventy-five more ways to be interrupted: The joke pool gains fifteen lines in each of its five tones - feelings, backlog, meta, craft and dark - for 842 lines in total. The shuffle bag still shows every filtered line once before repeating any, so the new ones arrive before the old favourites come back around.
- The bar shows where a swipe is going: Holding the main bar and dragging used to change tab on every step, so one swipe across three destinations popped and pushed the navigation graph three times: three page transitions under one finger, and the pages that were only passed through still started loading before being replaced. The pill now follows the finger and the page changes once, when you let go. Releasing on the tab you started from is not a page change at all, and an interrupted gesture navigates nowhere.
- Zoomed covers stay sharp: A poster was decoded at exactly the size it was drawn, which changed on every frame of a pinch. Each request cancelled the one before it, so the cover on screen stayed the one decoded at the previous size and was stretched over the growing tile until the fingers stopped. Posters are now decoded at a size that only changes in steps, always at or above the tile, so pinching in from the overview is sharp the whole way instead of settling into focus afterwards.
- The export says how far it has got: Rendering a tier list to an image fetches every cover on the board, and on a list of a few hundred titles that is long enough for a loading button to look stuck. The export sheet now draws a progress bar with a percentage that moves as each batch of posters arrives, so the wait has a shape and a size.
